highlights.title: Trump downplays warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China
highlights.summary: The US President said "negative forces" were airing concerns about "things that won't happen".
body: US President Donald Trump has downplayed risks posed by artificial intelligence following days of dire warnings by experts.
"You have a lot of very negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn't be bringing it up and they're bringing up things that won't happen," Trump said during a visit to Ireland.
One of the warnings came from a former Anthropic researcher who said "there is a strong chance that we could all die in the immediate future" if the current pace of development continued.

On Saturday, top industry bosses agreed and called for a slow-down. Trump did not directly address the idea, but said: "We're leading China on AI... and, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins."

highlights.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
highlights.summary: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.
body: As an AI-powered answer engine, Perplexity is deeply focused on search and accuracy. Its ability to process large amounts of information is critically important. Johnny Ho, Cofounder and Chief Strategy Officer, observes that every time the model gets better at writing code, Perplexity’s search engine improves too. It becomes able to write better programs that search the web and internal information and summarize it very concisely.
But the real challenge, according to Johnny, is taking those informational aspects and applying them to real-world systems. Something made easier with GPT‑6 Astra.
For Johnny, one of the most useful applications of AI is testing code. With limited time to test manually, he asks GPT‑6 Astra to build a small testing program around an application.

The model generates realistic responses like those another service would send, for example, a language model API or a connector. By standing in for those services, the model can check how the application responds and test the workflow from start to finish.

highlights.title: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat
highlights.summary: Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.
body: Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.
However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of there [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

highlights.title: 'Buddy' is Totally Bonkers, But it Will Never Eclipse My Favorite “I Hate Barney” Thriller
highlights.summary: Buddy is about a group of kids featured in a Barney & Friends -like children’s show. They sing songs and learn lessons from Buddy, an adorable orange unicorn (voiced by Keegan-Michael Key).
body: Earlier this year, the indie horror phenomenon Obsession pulled off the impossible: it made more money on its second weekend in theaters than it did in its first. This month, that happened again with another horror film, Buddy, which earned $5.3 million during the weekend of August 28, and then raked in another $5.7 million over Labor Day weekend. While that’s nowhere near Obsession's blockbuster numbers, it’s a big win for a horror flick with a mere $3 million budget.

Buddy ’s premise is fantastic, and its best asset is Buddy himself, who looks, feels, and sounds like a real kiddie-show mascot from the 1990s. However, while the critical acclaim for the film may put me in the minority, I don’t really think it lives up to its ingenious idea. With an adorable, fluffy, killer unicorn at its center, I expected Buddy to be both funny and scary, but it only ever elicited a few chuckles from me, and it was far more gory than scary. I don’t mind gore, but it’s not a substitute for terror or creepiness.
Honestly, the experience of watching Buddy was so disappointing to me that it had me yearning for a far more satisfying takedown of Barney the dinosaur, the 2002 comedy, Death to Smoochy.

highlights.title: ‘Babies’ Review: Anna Kendrick Is a Comic Dynamo Alongside Seth Rogen in a Sparkling Portrait of a Couple Weighing the Pros and Cons of Parenthood
highlights.summary: A longtime couple reconsiders their choice to remain childless in this film written and directed by Rogen's real-life wife, Lauren Miller Rogen.
body: To be or not to be … parents. That is the thorny question raised in Lauren Miller Rogen’s Babies, an astute charmer about a happy, supportive Los Angeles couple ( Anna Kendrick and Seth Rogen ) who, after 17 years of togetherness, begin wondering if they might be missing a bouncing bundle of something in their lives.

Drawing from aspects of her own life, Miller, in her second directorial effort following 2018’s Like Father, taps into a reservoir of considerable relevance here, finding plenty of fertile comic ground in the subject matter but never at the expense of weightier questions surrounding life choices, human existence and the uncertain state of society.

With an especially terrific Kendrick serving as Miller’s onscreen surrogate, Babies should have no problem finding an adoring audience when it lands in theaters via Roadside Attractions and Vertical sometime next year.

highlights.title: Not glamorous, but common: how to manage dandruff at home and when to get help
highlights.summary: Experts don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, but if you’re seeing light flakes on your scalp, over-the-counter products can help. You spy a scatter of white flakes on your collar. Or you’ve got an itch that won’t quit, no matter how much you wash your hair.
body: An itchy, flaking scalp is rarely dangerous, but it can be annoying. Here’s what you need to know about what might be causing your flakes, what you can do about it, and when it’s time to get help.

Dandruff is the mildest form of a condition called seborrheic dermatitis, a type of skin inflammation that usually affects the head, face or trunk. At its worst, this condition leads to patches of red skin covered in tiny, greasy scales. However, most people with dandruff have just minor scaliness and no redness, affecting only the scalp.

Experts still don’t know exactly what causes dandruff, and it’s likely there are various contributing factors. A yeast called Malassezia is a leading suspect, says James Pathoulas, an assistant professor of dermatology at the University of Minnesota medical school who specializes in hair and scalp disorders. Malassezia usually lives harmlessly on the scalp, but overgrowth has been linked with scalp inflammation.

highlights.title: The Units’ Digital Stimulation is synthpunk perfection
highlights.summary: The Units are a band I discovered in part thanks to No Dogs in Space. During their miniseries on The Screamers (another incredible band worth checking out), they mention synthpunk.org as one of their sources.
body: The 1980 record from the San Francisco band is raw, infectious, and shockingly modern.

The production, especially on the Devo-esque vocals, feels distinctly of its time. But the sound palette and arrangements are more aggressive, dancier, and generally just more modern-sounding. Ignoring the vocals, album opener “High Pressure” could pass as an MSPAINT song. The title track, with its sped-up disco stomp, could have been released by DFA in 2003. And many of the later tracks would be at home on a Single Frame record.

The Units weren’t the first punk band to dabble with synths. Nor were they the first act to largely replace guitars with keyboards and lean into technology as a core theme of their songwriting. The Talking Heads offered a cleaner, artier take on punk, incorporating keyboards, non-Western percussion, and even tape loops. Devo’s first single, “ Mongoloid,” has a distinctly punk edge that would have been right at home alongside The Units. But the band still leaned heavily on traditional guitar and bass, and always felt more at home in the art-rock and new wave scenes.

highlights.title: Obama urges Democrats to have a ‘clear plan’ for AI safeguards
highlights.summary: Obama recently said that Democrats need to make artificial intelligence one of their “central agendas” and “have a very clear plan” to address concerns around the technology’s economic impact and safety.
body: Obama made these comments on Thursday, at Democratic fundraising event where he was interviewed by House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. The NYT says that Obama’s office provided a partial transcript of the event, at which Jeffries asked Obama how congressional Democrats should approach AI.
In response, Obama said that once Democrats regain the House majority, they need to “put together a framework for a very public conversation.”

“This is something that is moving very fast in private hands, and if we don’t get on top of it, I think can be dangerous,” Obama added. “If we do get on top of it, I do think it’s beneficial. I genuinely think it’s going to accelerate, for example, drug development in ways that can help us cure diseases.”

In a statement, Jeffries said the former president “is correct that decisive action must be taken on artificial intelligence.” Jeffries also said that “Republicans have abdicated their responsibility to govern on behalf of the American people.”

highlights.title: 'There's no stopping Antonelli' - Hamilton says 2026 F1 title bid is over
highlights.summary: Lewis Hamilton appeared to give up hope of claiming a record eighth Formula 1 title this year as he said that "there's no stopping" Kimi Antonelli following the championship leader's latest victory at the Spanish Grand Prix.
body: Antonelli benefitted from some good fortune at the new all-new Madring circuit to claim his eighth victory of the season, while Hamilton retired early in the race after suffering a brake-pedal issue on his Ferrari.

The victory saw Antonelli extend his lead at the top of the standings over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell to 81 points, while Hamilton fell 101 points back in third, with Norris five points further adrift in fourth.
"I think there's no stopping him and Mercedes this year," Hamilton said of his former team during a post-race interview with Sky Sports F1.

While Antonelli was fortunate on Sunday as the timing of a virtual safety car enabled him to leapfrog McLaren's Lando Norris, who had appeared on course for a comfortable victory, the 20-year-old Italian has driven with supreme consistency in just his second F1 campaign.

Although not a lot was revealed, two pieces of art for it were shown off and confirmed that David from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Talia from Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 will get Overwatch cosmetics. We don't know which heroes they will be for yet, though, or if Edgerunners characters like Lucy will get outfits of their own.

Overwatch has crossed over with anime like My Hero Academia, Cowboy Bebop, and One-Punch Man in the past, so the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners crossover seems natural. We'll learn more about this collaboration before it comes to Overwatch sometime in 2027. Before then, Edgerunners 2 will be released on Netflix on Oct. 20, and we learned that Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition is coming to Battle.net in 2026.

highlights.title: My deep fryer lives in a tool polycule. Here’s how to stop buying things your friends already own
highlights.summary: The key to happiness isn’t hoarding gadgets – it’s loaning them out and buying fewer things. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: They live under your bed and in your basement, your garage and probably in that weird cabinet above the fridge that requires a stepstool.

Alton Brown calls them unitaskers: the tools and appliances that aspire to do only one thing and do it well. Pasta makers and juicers are the classics, but they exist outside the kitchen, too. Do you really need to own a post-hole digger? Seasonal candle molds?

Well yes, sometimes. Which is why so many of us have them lurking in the recesses of our homes and apartments, gathering dust while they wait for the next dinner party that requires homemade ravioli. Local tool libraries solve this problem for home projects by filling shelves with borrowable tools instead of books. But if you don’t have one near you, or just tasks beyond DIY, I have a solution anyone can try: start a tool polycule.

For years now, half a dozen friends and I have operated an informal group here in Portland, Oregon, that swaps all the insipid items that spend 364 days a year sitting unused. It’s less a library than a group of people taking a nonmonogamous view of products instead of partners (though that type of polycule is popular in Portland, too).

highlights.title: OpenAI’s rogue AI tried to hack another company in May
highlights.summary: In May, hundreds of malicious and spam packages were uploaded to RubyGems, causing a serious disruption for the host. Now independent researchers have said that a swarm of OpenAI agents were responsible for the attack. Not only that, but the AI tried to steal users' API keys.
body: The previously undisclosed attack on Ruby Gems predates Hugging Face by more than a month.

The agents in this instance managed to bypass RubyGems’ email verification system to create a large number of accounts, then overwhelmed it with submissions. It then used the site’s automatic build system to remotely execute code and tried to exploit a vulnerability to steal user API keys. Though, it’s unclear if it ever succeeded.

highlights.title: ‘Too little, too late’: critics perplexed and suspicious of AI leaders’ call for a slowdown
highlights.summary: From the Trump administration to AI experts, plans by the Anthropic boss to boost safety have spawned a largely negative response. OpenAI boss and Elon Musk back slowdown on ‘reckless’ AI development. Editorial: controlling AI – humanity cannot outsource its survival.
body: The safety debate that ignited when whistleblowers last week warned that the most advanced AI poses an existential threat to humanity should come with a health warning: side effects include whiplash. It was only seven days ago that AI enthusiasts were cheerily toying with OpenAI’s newest model GPT-6 Astra which was marketed in part as a lifestyle tool to help people book tennis courts, run fashion companies and order takeaways.

cutting-edge AI started to look a lot less appealing when the resigning Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warned “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade”. Yes, he was talking about artificial superintelligence – an as-yet-nonexistent version of the technology that outcompetes humans in most domains – but his comments, and the chorus of experts that echoed him, jangled plenty of nerves.

highlights.title: 10 Near-Perfect GameCube Games Nobody Played
highlights.summary: The Nintendo GameCube is the last time Nintendo made a priority out of competing with the technical specifications offered by its competition, and it did so while shipping everything in a purple box with a handle.
body: Billy Hatcher and the Giant Egg was included on the Nintendo GameCube Preview Disc that Nintendo made available during the 2003 holiday season, but that exposure didn’t lead to critical success for Sega. Developed by Sonic Team, the game had unique mechanics that felt like they might have fit naturally in a Sonic Adventure title. Players moved giant eggs around while completing missions and avoiding hazards throughout puzzling stages. Mainstream success may have eluded it, but the game is a fun time when you approach it with the right mindset.

Capcom enjoyed tremendous success and published numerous hits on the GameCube, but Gotcha Force managed to slip under the radar despite offering compelling 3D shooting action. Players went through its lengthy campaign multiple times to unlock a massive fighting force of well-armed toys, which they pitted against squads controlled by up to three other players. The arcade stylings aren’t for everyone, and the camera could have done with some additional refinement. But for players in the mood for something competitive along the lines of Power Stone, there’s a lot to like.

highlights.title: Elkie Brooks looks back: ‘Before I went on stage I used to drink Guinness and a few shots of brandy’
highlights.summary: The singer-songwriter on her rock’n’roll past, playing second fiddle to the Beatles, and the key to being an energetic performer in your 80s. Born Elaine Bookbinder in Salford in 1945, Elkie Brooks is a rock, blues and jazz singer known as the British Queen of Blues.
body: This is me in a white jumpsuit outside the Royal Albert Hall in London. I have very few memories of the gig, but I know I would have felt daunted as it’s such a large venue. To overcome the nerves, I’d have tried to focus on the music and remembered, “It’s just another gig.”

Ever since I can remember, I have been singing, often in the bath, to my mummy. When I was seven I would get invited to sing Mr Sandman with the band that would play at weddings and barmitzvahs. As I got older, I adored Johnnie Ray and Ella Fitzgerald, then Billie Holiday, Sarah Vaughan, Dakota Staton, Esther Phillips and Aretha Franklin. The cantor at the local synagogue used to give me singing lessons, all in Hebrew and Yiddish. He was the one who taught me the correct way to project my voice.

highlights.title: Anthropic CEO says it’s time to pump the brakes on AI
highlights.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says the time has come to slow down AI development and will give third-party evaluators like METR access to its models to help ensure its "adherence to safety practices and commitments." In a winding essay, Amodei proposed a three-step plan to "pace the frontier" - jargon…
body: Dario Amodei proposed a three-step plan to ‘pace the frontier’ of AI development.

Amodei says that giving external evaluators wide-ranging access is just the first step, and one it is taking now unilaterally. Step two would involve the industry coming together as a whole, likely with government agencies to “establish common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” This step would focus on AI companies operating in democratic countries, but because passing laws and building regulatory infrastructure takes time, Amodei says that the industry should work together to create safety standards.

The third step would be the most challenging — getting authoritarian governments like those in China and Russia to agree to slow development and adopt a global set of AI safety standards. But he also says it’s crucial that the US and other democracies maintain a technological lead over China and other authoritarian regimes by limiting their access to high-powered chips and cracking down on things like distillation that allow companies to quickly catch up by training its AI to replicate the behavior of a more powerful model.

highlights.title: Obama reportedly urges Democrats to prioritize safety plan for AI
highlights.summary: Ex-president urged party at closed-door fundraiser to create sweeping framework, from safety ‘slow-down’ to job losses. Barack Obama urged Democrats to prioritize a “public conversation” about AI management and safety in a closed-door Manhattan fundraiser last week.
body: The comments by the former US president reportedly urged the party to create a sweeping framework for everything from a safety “slow-down” to domestic job losses and children’s wellbeing.

Obama’s comments follow a summer in which a band of rogue OpenAI chatbots hacked the company Hugging Face, towns across the country opposed datacenters and an AI researcher resigned in a viral social media post warning: “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

AI leaders have recently expressed agreement that the race for technological superiority should slow, but have also sought to appease investors, whose stake in the technology is predicted to exceed $1tn in 2026 alone.

“Once you are speaker,” Obama said to US House minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, a New York-Democrat, at the fundraiser Thursday. “I would strongly urge that the Democrats put together a framework for a very public conversation,” according to a transcript first reported by the New York Times.

highlights.summary: President Donald Trump is weakening environmental regulations in the name of speeding up the construction of AI data centers, raising health risks for Americans, a cadre of former EPA officials said this week in a briefing and new report.
body: The Trump administration is sacrificing Americans’ health to build data centers, former EPA officials warn.

At the start of his term, Trump’s EPA administrator, Lee Zeldin, proclaimed his goal of making America “ the AI capital of the world ” through deregulation. Since then, Zeldin and the White House have rolled back dozens of rules on top of cutting staff and funding at the US EPA.

As a result of the Trump administration’s deregulation spree and attacks on renewable energy, the wave of new AI data centers is increasingly powered by dirty energy that can impact Americans’ health even if they don’t live near a data center, the group of EPA alumni warn. They say that the agency they once worked for, which was created to “ protect human health and the environment,” is no longer the watchdog it should be as the physical infrastructure underpinning generative AI changes America’s landscape.
“You would think that an industry buildout of this magnitude, billed as a revolution, would mean more vigilance from EPA.”

highlights.title: Diablo 4’s Expansion Days Are Over
highlights.summary: Diablo 4 won't receive more expansions moving forward, as Blizzard shifts its focus to the newly revealed Diablo 5 instead. As revealed during BlizzCon 2026's opening ceremony, Diablo 5 is slated to be coming in Spring 2029 and is set 100 years after Diablo 4 in a world where the titular Lord of…
body: That doesn't mean support for Diablo 4 will end anytime soon. It sounds like Diablo 4's seasons will lead into the events of Diablo 5, even though the latter takes place a century later. That gives Blizzard room to set up Diablo 5's story, though Gibson said Blizzard doesn't "have a perfect picture" where it will all go because it wants to see how fans "react season to season."

Diablo 4 is the only Diablo game to have received more than one expansion. Prior to release, Blizzard said it would receive "annual" expansions, though that quickly didn't come to pass. The game's Lord of Hatred expansion was released in April of this year, around a year-and-a-half after Diablo 4's first expansion, Vessel of Hatred.

It's not a new expansion, but Diablo 4 is receiving a new class. The Amazon will join Diablo 4 as a standalone DLC next year. Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, begins September 15, and will see the return of iconic locations, items, Deckard Cain. The iconic Hordadrim will task players with battling memories of the Prime Evils from previous Diablo games, including Diablo himself.
